# Investor køber to bombede aktier: “Griber en kniv, der falder”

**Feed**: borsen-podcast  
**Published**: 2026-08-26  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

The episode surveys where to invest after a strong European earnings season, contrasting two philosophies: Jens Rygaard buys momentum Nordic industrials (ABB, Sandvik, Wärtsilä) riding the electrification and AI-driven capex boom, while chief strategist Henrik Henriksen takes contrarian positions in beaten-down European automakers (Volkswagen, BMW). The panel flags stretched semiconductor valuations as the market's biggest risk (a potential AI-driven boom-and-bust rotation) and debates DSV's turnaround and the difficulty of picking defense winners like Kongsberg.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 WRT1V — Wärtsilä | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 75%

Jens's preferred Nordic AI/electrification play; broad exposure, gas turbines/baseload, shipping decarbonization, among leaders, has recovered well.

#### Reasoning

Jens bought and names Wärtsilä his top Nordic pick for the theme. Broad exposure beyond datacenters—baseload power to support renewable grids, gas turbines, and shipping decarbonization (EU net-zero 2050, port-access rules). Strong order intake across Nordic industrials (~33% growth, ~50% above expectations). Prefers paying for momentum and strong earnings over cheap stocks.

#### Sell Triggers

- if AI/datacenter capex boom slows broadly
- if global recession cuts industrial order intake
- if a more attractive earnings-momentum stock appears

> *"har jag egentligen ett gott öje till en som Vartila, alltså som, var du liksom får en lite bredare exponering"*

---

### 🟢 ABBN — ABB | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Jens bought into the investment boom; order growth ~33%, well above analyst expectations; broad electrification and grid-capex exposure.

#### Reasoning

Jens bought ABB as part of a Nordic industrial basket riding a violent investment boom. Q2 order intake up ~33%, ~50% above analyst expectations, broadly distributed. Global grid investment projected to rise from ~$400bn to ~$1000bn/yr, rippling to suppliers like ABB. Momentum priced in but Jens sees runway 'for a while yet'.

#### Sell Triggers

- if datacenter/AI orders fade
- if global recession hits industrial demand
- if valuation runs too far above historical range

> *"oavsett om du kikar på ABB eller Vartila som är inför två olika områden. Så det är som om det har kommit en gång i investeringslösten"*

---

### 🟢 SAND — Sandvik | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 65%

Bought by Jens as part of Nordic industrial basket exposed to the investment/electrification boom (mining, automation).

#### Reasoning

Jens named Sandvik among recent purchases in Nordic industrials benefiting from the broad capex boom (electrification, automation, mining, datacenter/energy). Same momentum thesis as ABB/Wärtsilä—strong, broadly distributed order growth, pay for momentum over cheapness. Less detail given specifically on Sandvik.

#### Sell Triggers

- if industrial order momentum fades
- if global recession reduces mining/automation capex

> *"Både svenska ABB och Sandvik och svenska Wärtsilä"*

---

### 🟢 VOW3 — Volkswagen | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 45%

Henrik bought a small (~1%) contrarian position; PE ~4, deeply out of favor; regulated turnaround, too big to fail, but negative momentum and ownership constraints.

#### Reasoning

Henrik took a small long-term contrarian position, likening it to his winning 2020 bank trade. VW trades ~4x earnings, ~1/3 of sales, cashflow positive; sector employs ~13.5m—'too big to fail'. But it's a regulated turnaround: Porsche/Piëch families, Lower Saxony (11.8%/20% votes) and IG Metall hold blocking power (80% supermajority law), risking incomplete restructuring. Long horizon, high risk.

#### Sell Triggers

- if German consumers shift to Chinese EVs
- if unions/Lower Saxony block restructuring
- if European auto follows British industry into decline
- global recession cutting consumer spending

> *"Det är ju att du griper en kniv som faller. Och det gör verkligen ont."*

---

### 🟢 BMW — BMW | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 45%

Henrik bought a small contrarian stamp; cheap 6-8x earnings, cashflow positive, but Chinese competition and negative momentum; German stimulus may help.

#### Reasoning

Henrik bought BMW alongside VW as cheap contrarian auto plays (6-8x current earnings, negative momentum). Cashflow positive, may benefit from German fiscal stimulus lifting employment/consumption and EV subsidies (up to €6,000/family). Risk: European auto slowly ground down by Chinese competitors who develop models far faster. Long-term, high-risk, small position; next move would be to add.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Chinese EVs win German home market
- if earnings/cashflow forecasts (not just revenue) get cut
- if European auto sector structurally declines
- global recession

> *"Han hade köpt ett lille frimärk i Volkswagen och BMW. Och det är ju några aktier som är lavt prissatt."*

---

### 🟢 DSV — DSV | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Jens holds a large position and bought more on the 15-20% dip; thesis rests on realizing ~DKK 9bn + 9bn Schenker synergies; historically superb at acquisitions.

#### Reasoning

Jens bought more; believes foreign investors wrongly lost faith. Thesis hinges on realizing the guided ~9bn (plus 9bn more from AI/IT integration) Schenker synergies—something DSV has historically executed superbly. Current ROIC is at post-financial-crisis lows (est. Q4 ~5.35% vs historical 15-16%), so re-rating requires the turnaround. Not a screaming buy on freight volumes alone; the Road division miss is the key risk.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Road division margin fails to recover ~1pp/week toward Q3
- if Schenker synergies don't materialize
- if ROIC stays depressed
- if it becomes just a normal logistics firm

> *"Jag har köpt lite mer, ja."*

---

### ⛔ NVDA — Nvidia | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Semiconductors at record ~16x price/sales (historical avg 4, low ~1x); high-beta cyclical; rising competition (OpenAI/Broadcom chip); Petersen&Partners underweight.

#### Reasoning

Henrik sees semiconductors as the market's biggest risk—trading ~16x sales vs historical avg 4 (mean-reversion implies -75%), never higher relative to revenue. Cyclical, high-beta, extremely volatile (10-20% daily swings), decelerating monthly revenue growth (~13% to ~10%). Fierce new competition (OpenAI/Broadcom chip beats it on power/efficiency). Firm is underweight; classic boom-and-bust risk, though likely a sector rotation not economy-wide crash.

#### Sell Triggers

- if monthly revenue growth reaccelerates and holds
- if supply stays constrained keeping pricing power
- if AI factory profitability proves durable

> *"Om de ska ner och handla det historiska genomsnittet, så är det 4. Då ska du skära 75 procent av kursen."*

---

### ⛔ KOG — Kongsberg | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 55%

Jens likes the defense megatrend but avoids Kongsberg—modern warfare has changed, gear may be obsolete, expensive after run-up; prefers cheaper/indirect plays.

#### Reasoning

Jens agrees European defense spending will rise but stays out of Kongsberg. Concern: warfare has fundamentally shifted (cheap drones defeat expensive systems; $10k drones vs $4m Patriots), so what's produced today may be obsolete post-Ukraine. Doesn't chase after a strong run-up; would rather find something cheaper or indirect (e.g., air-defense niche players). Acknowledges Kongsberg's missiles are relevant. Henrik plays the theme indirectly via banks/ETF instead.

#### Sell Triggers

- if valuation becomes cheaper after a pullback
- if it proves its product mix fits modern warfare
- confirmation of sustained order backlog (e.g. Patriot interceptor demand)

> *"du har ändå hållit dig bort från den norska försvarsaktien Kongsberg. Varför är det du är i tvivl om den aktien?"*

---
